title: Letters as vessels and garments: the letters of an idea, of desire and of thought

lectures.id: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3
Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

overview: Chapter 39 asks what it means that the letters of a thing are both a *kli* (vessel) and a *levush* (garment). The letters are a vessel because they define a thing: an idea, a feeling or a desire cannot be known as what it is without its letters, and those letters are part of its essence. They are a garment because they are external and can change: the same idea can be expressed in many ways, and no single expression captures its essence. The chapter shows this with the letters of the intellect, the letters of desire and emotion, the vessels of the ten *sefiros*, and the way thought clothes feelings and changes constantly from one thought to the next. The root of the letters is in the light that surrounds all worlds, the source of both the vessels and the garments. The same holds at every level of the chain of descent, up to the light of *Ein Sof*. The second class applies this to the Torah and mitzvos: the same essential commitment is expressed in many valid ways. A person must be flexible while deciding, then commit once the decision is made, because discipline becomes the vessel for free expression.

terms.gloss: the letters: the form in which an idea, a desire or a feeling is defined and expressed
the vessel: what defines and limits a thing, and is considered part of its essence
the garment: something external to the essence, separate from it, that can change
something; the tangibleness that defines and limits a thing so that it can be this thing
wisdom; the first flash of an idea

sections.title: Letters are a vessel and a garment at once
sections.summary: The letters of an idea or a feeling are its vessel (*kli*), part of its essence, and also its garment (*levush*), separate from it and changeable.

sections.title: Every idea comes with its own letters
sections.summary: When an idea goes out into the mind, its letters come with it. The letters are what define it, and each person expresses the same idea in his own letters and style.

They all arrive at the same point and the same intention, each in his own letters, as explained elsewhere.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Each idea has its own content, and it is also expressed in a way unique to the person who expresses it, like a snowflake. Nothing forces the idea into one set of words. The letters are part of that self-expression.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A cup, in the abstract and in actuality: he guesses this is philosophy. None of them is essential to the idea of a cup, yet an actual cup is impossible without some of them. In that sense they are part of the thing, made out of it, and yet external, since they could change.

sections.title: Desire, emotion and the vessels of the sefiros
sections.summary: The letters of desire and of emotion work as the letters of the intellect do. The vessels of the ten sefiros each have a form that defines them, though they reveal the same light.

phrases.en: and the same thing with the letters of desire or the letters of emotion

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: like for example, love in the heart,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: it's expressed

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and that's what's revealing it as something

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: בכמה אופנים שונים, כמו שכל אחד שמתגלה בצירופים שונים כו'
phrases.en: just like an idea can be expressed in many different ways, the feeling can be expressed in many different ways, but it has to be expressed in some way

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same holds for the letters of desire and of the *middos*. We know what we want, and what we feel, by a certain language of sensations. Take love in the heart: it feels a certain way, which may differ a little for a parent, a child or a spouse. Each feeling has its own expression, the sensations that make it what it is, and that is what reveals it as something. Some of those nuances are physical and some are emotional; without them you would not have the feeling.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Just as an idea can be expressed in many ways, a feeling can be expressed in many ways. But it has to be expressed in some way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that's called *kelim*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that's the *yesh*, the tangibleness that's defining and limiting

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: but it's considered part of the essence

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כמו כל בחינת כלים דעשר ספירות,
phrases.en: and this is like the *nimshal*, the idea of all the *kelim* of the ten *sefiros* is a similar thing

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כלי האור דחכמה וכלי האור דחסד ונצח וכהאי גוונא,
שהוא בחינת היש והתואר שלהם כו', כידוע

blocks.text: These letters are the *kli*. The expression is the light, and the way it is expressed is the vessel. The vessel is the *yesh*, the tangibleness that defines and limits the thing so that it can be this thing. It is considered part of the essence, because without it the thing would not exist and you could not know what it is.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The vessels of the ten *sefiros* are the *nimshal*: the idea of all of them is a similar thing. What makes *chachma* different from *bina*, and both from *chesed* and *gevura*?

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The vessels of the ten sefiros

blocks.text: All of them reveal G-d's essential light, and the real essence of that light is the same. G-d can reveal wisdom, the *bitul* in which everything is transparent to Him: everything is like nothing to Him. *Bina* reveals diversity. Those two concepts make *chachma* and *bina* separate things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Chesed* is creating something from nothing, and being totally dependent on a source outside us, which is an expression of G-d's *chesed*. *Gevura* hides that, so that we feel we have our own existence, our own consciousness and free choice.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Each *sefira* functions differently and creates in a different form, and that is what makes each one unique. G-d could have made the world with different logic and different ideas, and He chose these; in the Torah too He chose which things are logical, which are *g-dly*, and which are good or bad. That is the unique flavor of what exists. Energy is an example: we did not need energy to live, but G-d made us need it, and we get it by eating.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Behind everything there is an abstract idea, which is the light. To exist, it must have a specific form that defines it, and that form is the letters, which create the vessel for it. The light could have come into a different vessel.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Creation from nothing could have been expressed another way. The same goes for *netzach*: we depend on energy from the sun and on food, but G-d could have made us get our life in a totally different way. Some needs are readily available, like air, and others take effort, like food. G-d set each with its own level: what we need more of is more available, and what we need less of takes more work. That creates a unique experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Netzach* in a person is overcoming an adversary, but it is also perseverance: if I resolve to do something, I persevere even against external challenges. *Netzach* is a continuation of *chesed*. G-d creates us from nothing so we feel dependent on Him and grateful; *gevura* makes us feel independent; the physical world makes us feel separate. Yet even within nature we depend on things, such as the energy of the sun and food, and that dependence is how our dependence on G-d persists and overcomes the cover of nature.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: The vessel comes from the thickening of the light, and its root comes first
sections.summary: The vessel is the form that the light takes when it is made concrete, and its root comes before the lights. The same is true of the letters of the soul.

phrases.en: like we explained in chapter 28

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that the vessels are made from the thickening of the light

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and really the source of these vessels comes before the lights

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that's called the simple matter

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: קדם לשרש התהוות אור עצם הרצון והתענוג כו')
phrases.en: they come before the revelation of even the essential light, because the light has to be revealed to be created with letters

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The vessel is made from the thickening of the light, as explained in chapter 28. An abstract idea, like the concept of a cup, needs letters, specifics that define it. Philosophy calls these accidentals: they are external to the thing, yet the thing needs them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The root of the vessels comes before the lights; this is called the simple matter. Physically, you have a material and then give it a form. Here G-d has the essential ability of *gevura*, part of His *Ein Sof*: He is all-powerful and can limit Himself and choose these things. That is an essential self-expression, just like the light.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The source of the letters is part of the soul's essence, and it comes before the light is revealed, since the light must be revealed to be created with letters. Desire, pleasure, intellect and *middos* come from the soul's ability to have different movements. G-d's ability to limit Himself comes before any particular light, so the letters are a self-expression. The light reveals G-d only because it is all Him choosing to reveal Himself the way He wants.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Letters as garments that hide the essence
sections.summary: Once an idea is given its letters, the essence of the idea is clothed in them and hidden by them. The idea could be expressed in other letters, and no single expression captures its essence.

blocks.text: It is also true that the letters are called garments: a garment is something external to the essence, which can be changed.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A garment is completely separate from the essence, but the essence is clothed in it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Clothes that cover the person: the essence is put into the garment and expresses it, or is a symbol of it. Like your body, which you put clothes on. The clothes are not part of you and are something separate, but they express your style, and they cover you and hide you.

blocks.title: Clothes that cover the person

blocks.text: So too with the letters of the intellect. On the one hand, without a certain texture an idea could not be expressed at all. But once it is defined with certain letters or words, the essence of the intellect is clothed in them and hidden, since only the letters are revealed, just the way it happens to be expressed. It seems there is no other way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Teaching a child the color red: you show him one example, a Styrofoam cup, and he may think that this white cup is what a cup is. But who says a coffee mug is not called a cup? When an idea is expressed one way it seems to be the only way, but it could be expressed another way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Teaching a child the color red

phrases.en: But the truth is that the real essential, the essence of this idea, this concept

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: isn't specific to this form

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כי כמו לבוש יחליף ויתלבש באופני צירופים שונים אחרים לגמרי
phrases.en: because like a garment, the idea can change its expression and be revealed in completely different ways

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: וכללם אינם מגיעים בעצם מהותו כלל,
phrases.en: and even if you do it in a million different ways, all of them together will never fully express the essence of the idea

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: each of them is only one example, one expression, one revelation of the idea, but none of them fully capture the essence of it

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: (על דרך הנזכר לעיל באופני גלוי שכל וסברא אחד בלשונות המפרשים כו')
phrases.en: like we said before about how the different commentaries will express the same idea, each one of their own style

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The essence of this idea is not bound to this form; it could be expressed in a different one. So the letters hide the essence: like a garment, the idea can change its expression and be revealed in entirely different ways.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: However many ways you express an idea, none of them fully captures its essence, because it can be expressed in infinite ways. Each expression is one revelation of the idea. That is the relationship between the light and the letters.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: As we said before, the commentaries express the same idea each in his own style. If you learned it in one way, you might think that is the only way. But it could be expressed in infinite ways.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The duality: the idea needs a unique expression in letters and language, yet those letters limit it and make the manifestation seem to be the essence. The essence is more abstract and simpler, and can be expressed in infinite manifestations.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.1 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Desire and thought are garments that keep changing
sections.summary: One desire is clothed in many expressions, and thought is a garment that is constantly changed. The letters of the light and of the vessels have their source in the surrounding light, and the same three kinds of letters are in every level up to Ein Sof.

phrases.en: and you have a similar thing with the letters of desire, that our desire is also expressed like we said in *osios*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהרי רצון אחד פשוט מתלבש בכמה מיני גלויי אופנים שונים
phrases.en: that one, you can have the same essential simple desire and it becomes expressed in many different ways

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and it's just one, it's really just one *ratzon*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and just like the body will put on clothing, a garment that's external to it

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כך הרצון בא באופן גלוי שלו להחליף תמיד כו'
phrases.en: So too the desire becomes expressed in all different types of things, but those external expressions are just a garment to express the essential desire, what the person really wants

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The second class opens by picking up the chapter. The letters are both a vessel and a garment: an idea needs its letters to define it, and each person expresses the same idea in his own words, which is a garment, external to the essence of the idea and able to change.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Opening recap of class 39.2, placed under the first passage it returns to.

blocks.text: The same holds for the letters of desire. One simple desire is clothed in many different kinds of expression.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: It is still one desire. A person who wants honor may express it in many ways, but the essence of the wanting is the same.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person who wants money, or wants to be close to G-d, can express that one desire in many ways. Honor, money, closeness to G-d: each is one of the many forms the same desire takes.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Honor, money, closeness to G-d

blocks.text: So too the desire is expressed in all kinds of things, and those outer expressions are a garment for the essential desire, what the person really wants. The garment changes all the time.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person who wants a house: whether you live here or there does not matter. It is a different box for your things, but the essential desire, a place to feel at home, is the same.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The house

blocks.text: A person who wants to win, or to be kind, expresses that desire in many ways: different games, helping with shoes or coats, a smile or a kind word. The essential desire is the same.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Kindness in many forms

phrases.he: וכמו שאנו רואים באותיות המחשבה המלבישים למדות
phrases.en: like we see, like the letters of thought that are a garment to express a person's emotions, their feelings

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהאהבה שבלב שכבר באה באופן אותיות הגלוי שלה בלב,
phrases.en: so when a person has a feeling of love in the heart

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: when it comes up in thought

phrases.en: it's like a garment which is something separate from it

phrases.en: about this it says, that it's like a garment that's constantly changed

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ממש שהרי לבוש המחשבה אינו עומד אפילו רגע,
phrases.en: like we see that the thought never ceases, it's constantly running

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שתמיד פושט ולובש ופושט ולובש כו' ממחשבה למחשבה
phrases.en: is constantly taking off the old garment of the old thought and then putting on a new thought, and taking it off and putting on a new one

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כו' וכך גם אור השכל בבואו בלבוש דאותיות המחשבה,
phrases.en: The same thing with the intellect, that the same idea when it comes into letters of thought, the letters of thought become a garment that's constantly changed

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ממש פושט ולובש ממחשבה למחשבה כו'

blocks.text: The letters of thought are a garment that expresses a person's emotions. When love is in the heart, with its own letters, it rises into thought and is clothed in thought, as a body is in separate clothing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is why it says the garment of thought is constantly changed. Thought never stands still: someone in love thinks of the beloved this way and that, as in *Shir HaShirim*; someone angry replays what was said; someone worried runs through one thing after another. The old thought is taken off and a new one is put on.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same is true of the light of the intellect: when it comes into the letters of thought, it becomes a garment that is constantly changing, passing from thought to thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: When something is expressed on its essential level, its essential *ratzon*, idea or feeling has the letters that define it, and those are *kelim*. Expressed on an external level, such as *ratzon* into *sechel*, or any of them into *machshava* or *dibur*, it becomes a garment: a symbol that expresses it and can constantly change, and must, since that is how the essential thing is shown. Like teaching a child red with many examples, so that he finds the common denominator. The *yechida* and the other *koachos* are garments too. We express our connection to G-d by doing what He wants: keep Shabbos, or break it to save a life, or go to war on Shabbos if a *navi* says so. The readiness to move from one *avoda* to another shows an essential connection above the specifics.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן בחינת גלוי אותיות השכל בעצם הנזכר לעיל, שנחשב עם העצם
phrases.en: In contrast, the letters of the intellect itself when that's actually defining the idea, that's considered part of the essence

phrases.en: it's just that it appears like a *levush*, like the letters of thought once those letters are created, and then they become something separate from the

phrases.en: so it comes out understood from here, that they're both true

phrases.en: about the root of letters

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: sometimes they are *kelim*, they're a vessel

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: בהיותם בשרש מחצבם באחדות גמור עם העצם,
phrases.en: when they're in their root, in their source, where they're one with the essence

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל וגם הם נעשים בבחינת לבושים נפרדים מן העצם לגמרי,
phrases.en: and they also become these external *levushim*, these garments that are just manifesting the idea, that are separate from the essence

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and this is because the source of the letters are from the *makifim*, the idea of like *sovev kol almin*, the light that transcends a particular expression

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהן שרש הלבושים ומשם גם כן שרש בכלים המגבילים ומתארים
phrases.en: that is the source of the garments, but that's also the source of the *kelim* that limit and define things

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: like we explained before about how from the thickening of the light comes the *kelim*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and as is explained elsewhere

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The letters of the intellect itself, which define the idea, are considered part of its essence. What looks like a garment is the letters of thought, once they exist as something separate from the essence of the intellect.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Put into words, in Hebrew, Yiddish or English, the letters are a garment that can be expressed another way. But the idea needs an essential form of those letters to be defined, and that form is the *kli*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: So both are true: from the root of the letters, the letters are both *kelim* and *levushim*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Sometimes the letters are *kelim*: in their root, in their source, they are one with the essence. Sometimes they become *levushim* that are separate from the essence entirely, and therefore they can change.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The source of the letters is in the surrounding light (*makifim*). That source is the source of the garments, and also of the *kelim* that limit and define things, as explained elsewhere.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן למשכיל למעלה דרך כלל בכל בחינת לבושין דמחשבה דבור ומעשה,
phrases.en: and from this, from this explanation of the relationship of the letters to the light, somebody that is going to try to understand G-dliness can recognize the *nimshal* of the idea of the three *levushim* of *machshava*, *dibur*, *maaseh*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: these are three types of letters

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and these exist on every single level of the *seder hishtalshelus*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: all the way to the highest levels

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: all the way to the essential light of the infinite light

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: in the letters that were engraved there

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: the upper light

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and that is sufficient to understand

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: From this explanation, someone who tries to understand G-dliness can recognize the general point, the *nimshal*: there are three kinds of letters, of thought, speech and action, in every sefira of the chain of descent.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is on every level, from *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, through *Adam Kadmon*, the *ratzon kadum*, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. There are these different types of letters on every level. We will talk more about this in the coming chapters.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: All the way up to the highest levels, the essential light of the infinite light is revealed in the letters engraved there, in the upper light.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: He used to translate *tehiru ila'a* as "the upper purity", but he thinks another translation of *tehiru* is "light", and that "the upper light" is more accurate.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: He thinks the mashal is clear, and turns to how it relates to other things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Torah and mitzvos have an essential part and a part like a garment. When Moshe was shown the Torah at Har Sinai he was told forty-nine reasons to call a thing pure and forty-nine to call it impure; both are the words of the living G-d. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel differ on many things, and all the opinions are part of the Torah.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: The essence of the Torah is the readiness to do what G-d wants and to be committed to G-dliness, which can be expressed in many valid ways. Once a way is decided as the *halacha*, we follow it. Customs (*minhagim*) and different rabbanim are the same: different people do different things, and these are all valid ways of expressing that essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: We commit to one path though other paths exist, listening to the rulings "according to what they teach you", even when we feel the right should be the left. With *bittul*, that deference becomes an essential, G-dly expression.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: When a rav debates and both sides are valid, they have to look at it. *Minhag hamakom*: do it the way they do it in the place you are, as long as it is for the sake of Heaven. That *bittul* lets the essence plug into something external.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: The *pnimiyus haTorah* brings out the essence and spirit of the law, its *kli*; the external practice is a garment. Plugged in with the right perspective, it takes on the quality of the essence: doing Torah and mitzvos with *bittul* and the joy of a mitzva.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Be careful and flexible while deciding, see the merit of all the sides, and then commit. He heard from many people that the Rebbe would deliberate for a long time before starting something new, but once he decided, he did not change his mind.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.
blocks.question: Should I be decisive, or should I be flexible?

blocks.title: Can we do this?
blocks.text: A parent or a teacher often hears a child ask, 'Can we do this?' From a more mature perspective it does not really matter how it is done; it is not essential. There are different considerations for how to decide.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: What is essential is that once we decide, we commit and follow through, with *bittul*. Once we agree to certain rules or a system, we must be very careful before changing or compromising on it. Firm limits outside our control, the idea of *malchus*, are called the *kos shel bracha*, the cup that holds blessings.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Discipline comes before freedom. To learn a language you first learn the vocabulary and grammar, and then you can express yourself. The same with writing and with an instrument: the scales come first, and then practice becomes the vessel for free expression.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.
blocks.title: Discipline before freedom

blocks.text: A *Hayom Yom* entry, which he thinks is from 25 Shevat, says that human laws are created by life, but the Torah creates life.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Society and times change, and in some ways the Torah, halacha and *minhagim* have changed with them. But much of it is like the rules of a game: it does not really matter how you do it. No system is perfect, as the Rambam says in the *Moreh Nevuchim*. I can thrive in any system if I am willing to learn it, master it and be flexible: it is more important to develop my talents within a system than to change the system to make it easier and be lazy.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: The Torah's fixed structure forces us to go inside ourselves, against the currents of our society, and become creative, G-dly people with an inner moral compass. It gives us the power to change ourselves and the world around us.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: A false kindness, lenient with oneself or a child, so that the rules are changed for them, like is happening a lot in our society today, is detrimental. It stops the person from developing the skills to reach their potential.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping remark about present-day society, a jab at the culture rather than a point about the halacha.
sensitivity.publishable: A false kindness, lenient with oneself or a child, so that the rules are changed for them, is detrimental. It stops the person from developing the skills to reach their potential.

blocks.text: On the one hand these are external things that can change and come in many ways; once we plug into them, they become an essential *kli*. To answer the question, before doing something be flexible and consider every option. Once committed, be very careful about changing it, to be sure the change does not come from laziness.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: If a child really cannot do something, you should make an exception for them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: If a person really needs a *heter*, a good rav is going to give them one, but be careful not to rob them of the pressure they need to be successful and excellent.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

sensitivity.publishable: If a person really needs an exception, one can be made, but be careful not to rob them of the pressure they need to be successful and excellent.

blocks.text: Sometimes that pressure is positive, even if at first it is a little bit of *gevura*. That is the challenge with these things.

blocks.text: Now and then we make a *cheshbon hanefesh*, or ask a *mashpia* or a rav. We cannot do that every day, since second-guessing our choices stops us from acting.

blocks.text: There are set times for a *cheshbon hanefesh*: Rosh Hashanah, a birthday, or once a week on Thursday night, to reconsider our priorities and our direction in life.

blocks.text: Most of the time we must commit to action, because only action gets things done. Sometimes acting imperfectly is better than never acting for fear of being wrong.

blocks.text: Souls come from the letters of *machshava*, and angels from the letters of *dibur*. A soul has a *chelek Elokah*, one with G-d, and a personality, which is an external garment that can change.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Every person has an essence that does not change; the *koachos*, sechel and middos, which develop but do not totally change; and the garments of *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh*, which change completely. From a higher view, even the *koachos* are a garment to the soul's essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: On every level, what is essential on one level is a garment compared with a higher level. That is the basic idea to understand.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: The same with the *sefiros*: on one level they are essential, and on another level they are like a garment, because G-d could have chosen other *sefiros*, or things that are not *sefiros* at all.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class goes on past line 42 to apply the mashal to Torah, mitzvos and the sefiros; placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Within each *sefira*, the logic and reason of the 613 mitzvos, which G-d creates, is like a garment. G-d could have made other things make sense, and those would have made sense to us.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: G-d sets up the system and plugs His essence into it, and then it is essential. Seen one way, G-d is higher than these things; seen another way, at a certain level they become essential. Gravity could have worked differently, but it does not, and we live in this reality.

blocks.text: Once we learn these ideas we must go back and revise our understanding of the earlier levels, such as the *ratzon kadum* and the *igulim* that go into *yosher*: a similar process of the essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 39/039 Shaar HaYichud ch 39.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The *igulim* are like the essence and the *kelim*, and when they come into *yosher*, that is like a garment for them. The same is true in *Atzilus* and everything like that.

reviewQuestions.question: Why are the letters of an idea both a *kli* and a *levush*?
What does the living creature show about the essential life that is expressed in movement?
How can one desire come out in many different expressions, and still be the same desire?
Why do the sefiros differ from one another, if they all reveal the same light?
Why is the essence not the same as its garments, and why do the garments of the soul keep changing?
How should one balance flexibility and commitment, in deciding and in acting?
